steps.text: I'm June, Maya's aunt. Her birthday is this week and I want to give her $300. Should I just send her the cash? She's on SSI, and her family made a Giftwise page for her: maya.

Gift page for Maya (/g/maya). Open needs: Wheelchair repair: $420 still needed, paid to Riverside Mobility Repair; Laptop for college: $649 still needed, paid to Eastgate College Bookstore; Electric bill, November: $138 still needed, paid to Maya's ABLE account; Therapy co-pay: $90 still needed, paid to Northside Physical Therapy. Any amount can also go to her ABLE account.

Cash counts as income. $300 minus $80 in exclusions leaves $220 counted in November, so their January check would be $774. Giving the item itself keeps $994. Sources: 20 CFR 416.1121: types of unearned income, including gifts; POMS SI 00830.520: Gifts; POMS SI 00810.410: Infrequent or Irregular Income Exclusion; POMS SI 00810.420: $20 General Income Exclusion; POMS SI 02005.001: Retrospective monthly accounting.
$300 for Maya: $300 to Riverside Mobility Repair (Wheelchair repair). Her check stays $994. Given as cash, it would be $774.

June, I'd hold off on sending cash. Social Security counts a cash gift as income. After $80 in exclusions, $220 of your $300 would count, and her January SSI check would drop from $994 to $774. So the gift would cost her $220.

Instead, I suggest putting the full $300 toward her wheelchair repair. Giftwise would pay Riverside Mobility Repair directly, and her check would stay at $994. The repair still needs $420, so this is a big help. Other options on her page: the laptop for college, a therapy co-pay ($90), or her ABLE account.

Would you like me to set up the $300 payment to the wheelchair repair? Once you say yes, I'll send you a PayPal link to approve. Nothing is paid until you approve it yourself.
That makes sense. Yes, please set up the $300 that way.

PayPal checkout ready for $300 to Maya, paid to 1 recipient. The person giving should open this link and approve in PayPal: [PayPal approval link]. After they approve, the receipt will be at /r/[receipt].
